JEEM: Vision-Language Understanding in Four Arabic Dialects

paper.arxiv.2503.21910

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2503.21910v1. Four-region native-speaker annotation and dialect-coverage limits establish construction/QC scope. Exactv1identity preserved; regional sampling does not establish broad Arabic representativeness. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

JEEM covers four dialects with an uneven, relatively small image set; automatic metrics may miss cultural/dialect nuance and human evaluation covers only a subset.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

JEEM separates dialect-first captioning from question writing without access to the image, then answers questions with the image and captions; team leaders review submissions and may edit, reject or reassign them.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

JEEM contains 2, 178 images and 10, 890 question-answer pairs across Jordanian, Emirati, Egyptian and Moroccan Arabic; native-dialect recruitment yields teams of 10, 8, 10 and 9 annotators respectively.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

On the sampled Jordanian image-caption evaluation, Table 3 reports human-rated dialect authenticity of 3.56 for GPT-4o captions and 4.82 for reference human captions on a 1–5 scale; human evaluation uses 50 images per dialect and one blinded rater per caption.
